method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All nineteen translated content blocks, including the source-commented explanatory and exercise blocks.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: To reduce enumeration of B to enumeration of A, a surjection A-to-B transforms any enumeration x_1,x_2,... of A into f(x_1),f(x_2),... of B.
samples.checks: The reduction direction, surjection direction and both enumerated sets are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assume Pow(Nat) enumerable and map each N to its unique binary characteristic sequence s, with s(n)=1 exactly when n is in N and 0 otherwise.
samples.checks: OLSIZ-010 removes only the unbound k and uses s/s(n) consistently; an adjacent note and projection QA record the delta.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The characteristic-sequence map is a function and is surjective because every binary sequence determines the set of positions at which it contains 1.
samples.checks: The even/empty/full examples, set-builder inverse witness and equality f(N)=s remain intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Applying f to the assumed list of all subsets lists every binary sequence, which contradicts the prior nonenumerability theorem and proves Pow(Nat) nonenumerable.
samples.checks: Surjectivity, list construction, cited theorem and contraposition conclusion remain explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercises request reductions for Nat-to-Nat functions, sets of pairs, infinite natural sequences, binary surjections and the reals.
samples.checks: Every active problem retains its set, function type and nonenumerability conclusion; commented source material remains commented.
